[QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | An alternative meaning of zakā is to become sound or righteous, from zakā yazkū zakāʾ.
[QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن وأبو حيوة | reports | Al-Hasan and Abu Haywa read the verb with a geminated kāf: God alone purifies, guides, and cleanses people by His favor, not through their deeds.
[QURTUBI-FULL:24:21-22/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisaʾi treats the prohibition against following Satan as parenthetical; “none of you would ever be purified” answers both that clause and the preceding “were it not for God’s favor.”
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Repeating the mention of God's favor and mercy recalls His delay of punishment, underscoring the offense's gravity.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:18-21/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The clause that God is compassionate and merciful is coordinated with His favor; the conditional answer is omitted because already stated.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Here following Satan's steps means spreading indecency.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | The word is also read with an open ṭāʾ; Nāfiʿ, al-Bazzī, Abū ʿAmr, Abū Bakr, and Ḥamza read it with sukūn.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The following clause explains why following Satan is prohibited.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Fāḥishah is extreme ugliness.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Munkar is what religious law rejects.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | God's favor includes enabling repentance that erases sins and prescribing penalties that expiate them.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Zakā means purification from the stain of sin, forever.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | God purifies whom He wills by guiding that person to repentance and accepting it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:24:21-22/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | God hears what they say and knows their intentions.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Satan’s steps are his traces and whispers, followed by listening to the slander and talking about it.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Fahshāʾ is what is extremely vile.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Munkar is what people’s souls reject, recoil from, and disapprove.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Without God’s favor and mercy in granting expiatory repentance, none would have been purified of the slander’s sin thereafter.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God purifies those who repent by accepting their sincere repentance.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p139#5/r6] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God hears what people say and knows their inner selves and sincerity.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The expression 'steps of Satan' was previously explained, including its readings, in the commentary on al-Baqara. | mentions 2:168
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The pronoun in 'he commands' returns to the conditional 'whoever'; fahsha is extreme ugliness, and munkar is what sound minds reject.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Without God's favor and mercy through purifying repentance, none would be purified.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read ma zaka with a light kaf; several other readers double the kaf and some apply imala.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p24#2/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | God purifies whom He wills, either those destined for felicity, whose good works signal it, or those whose sincere repentance He accepts.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أبو البقاء | reports | Abū al-Baqāʾ begins with parsing the pronoun as the pronoun of the matter.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A second parse makes the pronoun refer to Satan.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A third parse makes the pronoun return to the conditional relative man, whoever follows Satan.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | The matter-pronoun and Satan-reference parses are valid only for grammarians who do not require the conditional noun to have a resumptive pronoun in the answer clause.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الجمهور | reports | The majority read the kāf lightly, from zakā yazkū; its final alif is read with or without imāla.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الأعمش وأبو جعفر | reports | Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read the kāf doubled. The alif is written as yāʾ unusually, either reflecting imāla or spelling the doubled reading.
[SAMIN-DURR:24:21/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | With the light reading, min aḥadin is the subject; with the doubled reading it is the object. Min is extra in either parse, and God is the subject in both.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God hears His servants' words and knows which of them deserves guidance or misguidance.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r10] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو رافع | reports | Abu Rafi reports that Ibn Umar, Zaynab bint Umm Salama, and Asim ibn Umar all judged his wife's conditional vows to become Jewish or Christian and free her slaves a satanic impulse, not grounds to divorce.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r11] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Without God's favor, no one would attain purity or good: God grants repentance and return, purifying souls from association, immorality, and bad traits to differing degrees.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r12] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | God purifies whom He wills among creation and misguides and casts whom He wills into the hazards of error.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The devil's footsteps are his ways and paths, and what he commands.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The warning is expressed in language Ibn Kathir describes as exceptionally clear, concise, forceful, and beautiful.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains the devil's footsteps as his deeds.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · عكرمة | reports | Ikrima explains the devil's footsteps as his incitements or insinuations.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says every sin belongs to the devil's footsteps.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · أبو مجلز | reports | Abu Mijlaz counts vows to commit sins among the devil's footsteps.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r8] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن مسعود | reports | When a man vowed to abstain from food, Ibn Masud called this a satanic impulse and told him to expiate his oath and eat.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p30/r9] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · الشعبي | reports | When a man vowed to slaughter his son, al-Shabi called it a satanic whisper and instructed him to sacrifice a ram.
[BURHAN:v4p375/r8] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | When the response to لولا is negative, Qur'anic usage omits it; this contradicts Ibn Asfur's claim that a negative with ما is better accompanied by لام.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | One who follows Satan takes on his deeds and sinks to utter baseness; spelling out Satan again makes the warning stronger than a pronoun would.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The believers are urged to make every effort not to imitate Satan or follow any path he beautifies; the verb form also hints at pardon for inadvertent slips.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The repeated explicit phrase, instead of a pronoun, heightens aversion; following Satan is framed as deliberate resolve rather than mistake or forgetfulness.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p246/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Satan commands extreme ugliness and whatever the law does not permit; he aims first at the greatest deviation and descends to lesser evil if thwarted.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · a

uthor | holds | God's favor purifies souls and lifts them above base desires, while His mercy grants repentance that expiates the deficient speech and low actions ignorance caused.

[BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God alone purifies whom He wills from the soul's impurities and heart's diseases: He protected some from the slander and left others to fail.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p247/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God hears every utterance and knows thoughts, states, and deeds, so He knows who is fit for purification; believers should thank Him and patiently continue kindness toward others.
[DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r10] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · author | holds | God makes righteous whomever He wills.
[DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · author | holds | The footsteps of Satan mean Satan's embellishment and enticement.
[DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · author | holds | Fahisha means sins; munkar means what is not recognized as right, such as the accusation made against Aisha.
[DURR-FULL:v6p153#2/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · author | holds | Zaka means becoming righteous: without God's favor and mercy, none of them would ever have become righteous.
[ITQAN:v2p323/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Mā zakā minkum means “none of you was guided.”
[ITQAN:v2p510#2/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | As an exception-preventing particle, lawlā enters a nominal clause; a positive answer takes lām, a negative answer does not, and a following pronoun should be nominative.
[ITQAN:v2p510#2/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Lawlā can mean halā as exhortation or offer with a present verb, or express rebuke and regret in other contexts.
[ITQAN:v2p510#2/r3] ITQAN, d. 911 · الهروي | reports | Al-Harawī lists an interrogative use of lawlā, but the author says the cited examples more likely mean halā.
[ITQAN:v2p510#2/r4] ITQAN, d. 911 · الجمهور | rejects | Al-Harawī treats lawlā in فلولا كانت قرية آمنت as negation, but the majority reject that analysis and read the verse as rebuking failure to believe before punishment, supported by Ubayy's هلا reading.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | In min kum min ahad, the first min is explanatory; the second is extra, and ahad is nominative as the subject.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r10] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The practical counsel is to spend from lawful earnings, associate with jurists and wise people, and avoid the ignorant and sinful.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r11] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | Some interpret Satan’s steps as vows to disobey God; vows to obey, such as prayer or fasting, are excluded because they prevent indecency and wrong.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r12] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Purification ultimately belongs to God, who enables obedience by grace, yet a student needs a teacher to learn purification according to God’s intent; the Prophet is the greatest means.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r13] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · عبد الله الأنصاري | reports | Abdullah al-Ansari says he had many hadith and law teachers, but Abu al-Hasan al-Kharaqani taught him the spiritual path; without meeting him, he would not have known reality.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r14] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · عبد الله الأنصاري | reports | Spiritual guides lead along the religious path and unlock certainty; the perfected human’s presence and companionship are a great blessing.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Abadan means for all time, without end.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God purifies whom He wills by bestowing the effects of grace and mercy, guiding the person to repentance and accepting it, as He did for them.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The verse refutes the Qadariyya, who claim souls are purified through acts of worship without God’s enabling.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God hears their words, including the slander and their expressed repentance, and knows their intentions; this urges sincere repentance.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Satan’s many steps encompass every indecency and wrong, including slander, insults, lies, and searching out people’s faults.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الحديث | reports | A hadith says human speech is against its speaker except speech commanding right, forbidding wrong, or remembering God.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الحديث | reports | A hadith calls it great treachery to tell a brother something he trusts while lying to him.
[BURSEVI:v6p93#2/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الحديث | reports | A hadith praises the person whose own faults keep him occupied instead of other people’s faults.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God’s immense generosity and mercy purify people of blameworthy traits despite their deserving punishment; He created them for mercy, while punishment follows their bad choices.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | With damma, khutwah is the distance between the feet; with fatha, one stride. Following footsteps idiomatically means adopting someone’s way, here Satan’s course.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Believers must not follow paths Satan whispers into their hearts and beautifies to their eyes, including spreading or cherishing scandal.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Fahshaʾ is what is extremely ugly by custom or reason, in word or deed; munkar is what the Law rejects, while Abu Layth says it is unknown to scripture and sunnah.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · أبو الليث | reports | Abu Layth defines munkar as what is not recognized in a revealed law or the Sunna.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · المفردات | reports | Al-Mufradat includes what sound reason deems ugly or leaves undecided, provided the Law judges it ugly.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Calling Satan’s beautifying and goading an “order” belittles the followers who heed him.
[BURSEVI:v6p93/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God’s favor includes these explanations, enabling repentance that erases sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate them; without this, no one would be purified.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Following Satan's footsteps is a metonym for following him and obeying his whispers in every action and omission, including spreading and desiring indecency.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | زكى means becoming purified from the stain of sins.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · نافع والبزي برواية ابن ربيعة وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة | reports | These readers pronounce the ṭāʾ of خطوات with sukūn; another reading has fatḥa.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | In both readings, خطوات is the plural of خطوة, the distance between the feet; خطوة with fatḥa on khāʾ is instead the verbal noun of stepping. The plural normally moves the medial vowel to distinguish a noun from an adjective.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Repeating the explicit nouns instead of saying ومن يتبعها or من يتبعه intensifies and reinforces the warning.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | الفحشاء is what is extremely vile; المنكر is what religious law condemns.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The pronoun in فإنه can refer to Satan or to the matter; one analysis posits an omitted conditional answer supplied by what follows, originally explaining the prohibition. Grammarians object that answers are omitted only after past conditions, citing a line beginning لئن تك قد ضاقت علي بيوتكم; the response is that here the following clause itself stands in the answer's place.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو حيان | reports | Abu Hayyan says the pronoun refers to the conditional clause, with no ellipsis: whoever follows Satan becomes a leader in misguidance who commands indecency; this assumes a nominative conditional answer must contain a returning pronoun.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God's favor includes the clear revealed signs, guidance to repentance that cleanses sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate sins other than apostasy according to a group of scholars.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p123#3/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · جمع | reports | A group holds that legal penalties expiate sins other than apostasy; they answer the earlier Abu Hurayra report by saying it predates revelation of this ruling to the Prophet.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · روح والأعمش | reports | Ruh and al-Aʿmash read زكى with gemination and imāla.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The ungeminated زكى is written with yāʾ despite its wāw root because it can undergo imāla or by analogy with the geminated form, as Abu Hayyan notes.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | منكم is explanatory; من أحد is extra for emphasis. أحد is nominative as subject in one reading, but accusative as object in the other, with God as its subject.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | أبدا means ever, without an endpoint.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God purifies whom He chooses by granting grace and mercy, enabling repentance and accepting it, as He did with those involved in the slander who were free of hypocrisy.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God hears all speech, including their expressed repentance, and knows all things, including their intentions.
[ALUSI-FULL:v18p124/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The verse urges sincer

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Coming after the ten verses about the slander, this warning identifies their prohibitions, evil suspicions, and wish to spread indecency as satanic whisperings.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p186/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The command depicts satanic whispering as Satan walking and a person obeying as following his steps, making an unseen mental influence into a perceptible scene.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Without God's guidance to good and forgiveness upon repentance, no person would attain purity: Satan's trial is formidable and few could escape it unaided by religious guidance. | mentions 38:82, 38:83
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The familiar reading has a light kāf; the word ends in wāw and has no imālah, so its expected spelling is a plain alif although the muṣḥaf draws the alif in yāʾ form.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187#2/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | This spelling does not conflict with the muṣḥaf: only a change to the pronounced letters would do so, while transmission safeguards performance.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr read ṭāʾ with sukūn; the other readers vocalize it with ḍamma, also a common permissible form.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | A khuṭwah is one step: moving the foot that trailed behind forward past the other foot. | mentions 2:168
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Man is conditional here, so all readers agree that yatbaʿ is jussive.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The clause beginning fa-innahu is the conditional response; its link is the omitted general object of “commands,” which includes the one who follows Satan, and both pronouns refer to Satan.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Anyone following Satan's way falls into indecency and wrong, since Satan commands people to commit both and the follower is included in that general address.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-faḥshāʾ is any ugly deed or utterance. | mentions 2:169
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p187/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-munkar is what the revealed law and people of virtue reject. | mentions 3:104
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The closing dictum joins promise and threat: God hears those spreading indecency and knows their wish to do so, and hears and knows those who condemn it, rewarding each for their deeds.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p188/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Naming God explicitly makes the closing statement stand on its own like a proverb.

[TABATABAI:24:20-22/r10] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | God is hearing of the request for purification and knowing of the person’s readiness for it.
[TABATABAI:24:20-22/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his commentary on the parallel command in 2:208. | mentions 2:208
[TABATABAI:24:20-22/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The repeated appeal to grace, now explicitly answered by ‘none would be purified,’ reflects that God alone bestows goodness and salvation; the Qur’an says good is in His hand and good that reaches people is from Him. | mentions 3:26, 4:79
[TABATABAI:24:20-22/r9] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | God wills to purify those prepared for purification who ask for it through their state of readiness; He hears their request and knows their preparedness.
